title: Buried with him (Romans 6:3–4)
hookLine: baptized into his death to walk in newness of life

cards: In some old churches, the baptismal font isn't a basin. It's a pool set into the floor, with steps going down one side and up the other. Some are even shaped like a tomb, or a cross.
You walk down into the water, go under, and come up the other side. Nobody designed that by accident. The shape is a sermon in stone, and it comes from two verses in Romans 6.

teach.h: SHALL WE SIN THAT GRACE MAY ABOUND?
teach.b: Paul has just said that where sin abounded, grace abounded more. Someone might say: great, then let's keep sinning so there's more grace. Paul's answer: God forbid.
And then, in the Douay-Rheims: "Know you not that all we, who are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death?"
The Greek word baptizo means to dip or plunge, to immerse. Paul sees baptism as a plunge into Christ's own death and burial.
Verse four: "For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life."
The old self goes down into the water the way a body goes into a grave.
And as Christ came up from the tomb, the baptized come up to walk, step by step, in a life that's new. Not a fresh coat of paint on the old one.
That's why the Church baptizes new members at the Easter Vigil, the night between Christ's burial and his rising. Why the newly baptized are handed a candle lit from the Easter candle.
And why there are fonts with steps down and steps up.
Whether a person is immersed in a pool or has water poured on the head, Catholics believe the same thing happens: dying and rising with Christ. Someone baptized as an infant doesn't remember it.
Paul writes as though it shapes every step after.

how: Catholics bless themselves with holy water as they enter a church, recalling their baptism, and Romans 6:3–11 is the Epistle read at the Easter Vigil, the night new members are baptized.

games.q: someone says: if grace abounds where sin abounds, why not keep sinning and get more grace? you're Paul. what do you say?
o: God forbid: you were baptized into his death, to walk in new life.
games.why: Paul says God forbid, and asks if they don't know they were buried with Christ by baptism, so as to walk in newness of life.

practice: Touch some water with your fingers: holy water by a church door, or any tap or glass will do.

Catholics make the sign of the cross with it, remembering their baptism; if that's not your practice, feel the cool of it and think of one old habit you'd leave in the water, and one step of new life you'd take.
Let it dry on your skin.

wordCard.voice: Baptizo. The Greek word for plunge or immerse: Paul's picture of baptism as a burial with Christ, and a rising to newness of life. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: to dip, plunge or immerse. Paul hears in it a burial and a rising.

carryVoice: Your line: newness of life. The old self stays down in the water. Until tomorrow.
